Purpose: test the three predictions in documents/model-design.md §5 before any

```{r setup}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(tidyverse)
library(lmerTest)
library(here)
library(broom.mixed)
library(knitr)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))

color_map <- c(
  "No Competitor" = "#FCAD12FF",
  "Within Trial"  = "#85216BFF",
  "Across Trial"  = "#CB4149FF"
)

old_conditions      <- c("noncomp", "comp-within", "comp-between")
new_conditions_long <- c("No Competitor", "Within Trial", "Across Trial")

final_game_set <- "run_v3"
data_root      <- here("data", "processed_data", "exp_1")
fig_path       <- here("analysis", "figures")

# Exp 1 exclusions, reproduced from 03_setup-annotations.R rather than sourced,
# so this notebook stays read-only.
game_blacklist <- c(
  "01JGZ1J4WKTCRGQS8R8214JJH2", # AI response
  "01JGMPEGCD0EX4TXSSNEY3A670"  # AI response
)

FINAL_BLOCK <- 3  # repNum is 0-indexed; 4 blocks of 16 trials
```

## 1. Load

Note the data path. The published notebooks use
`here("data", "processed_data", final_game_set)`; the processed data has since
moved under `exp_1/`, so the path here is
`here("data", "processed_data", "exp_1", final_game_set)`. The published
notebooks have not been updated, deliberately — Exp 1 is frozen.

```{r load}
#| message: false
load_data <- function(data_name) {
  files <- list.files(
    path       = file.path(data_root, final_game_set),
    recursive  = TRUE,
    pattern    = paste0("^", data_name, "\\.csv$"),
    full.names = TRUE
  )
  stopifnot(length(files) > 0)
  map_dfr(files, read.csv)
}

d_game   <- load_data("games")
d_round  <- load_data("rounds")
d_chat   <- load_data("chats")

# 205 MB / ~970k rows. text1 and text2 are long strings and are not needed here;
# dropping them on read keeps the swap-and-bind in §2 from doubling them.
d_chat_similarity <- readr::read_csv(
  file.path(data_root, "message_similarities.csv"),
  col_select = c(gameID, roundID1, roundID2, similarity),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

d_game <- d_game |>
  mutate(contextStructure_f = factor(contextStructure,
                                     levels = old_conditions,
                                     labels = new_conditions_long),
         contextStructure_f = relevel(contextStructure_f, ref = "No Competitor"))
```

### Exclusions

Reproduces the published filter. The assertion is the guard: if this stops
returning 450 dyads, something upstream has changed and every number below is
suspect.

```{r exclusions}
game_stats <- d_round |>
  left_join(d_game |> select(gameID, contextStructure, contextStructure_f),
            by = "gameID") |>
  group_by(gameID, contextStructure, contextStructure_f) |>
  summarize(n_correct  = sum(correct, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_responses = sum(!is.na(response)),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n_responses > 0) |>
  mutate(non_response_rate = n_responses < 32,
         inaccuracy        = n_correct / n_responses < .75,
         blacklist         = gameID %in% game_blacklist,
         kept_game         = !non_response_rate & !inaccuracy & !blacklist)

kept_games <- game_stats |> filter(kept_game) |> pull(gameID)

game_stats |>
  filter(kept_game) |>
  count(contextStructure_f, name = "n_dyads") |>
  kable(caption = "Dyads retained by condition")

cat("Total kept dyads:", length(kept_games), "\n")
stopifnot(length(kept_games) == 450)
```

```{r filter}
d_game_f  <- d_game  |> filter(gameID %in% kept_games)
d_round_f <- d_round |> filter(gameID %in% kept_games)
d_chat_f  <- d_chat  |> semi_join(d_round_f, by = "roundID")
d_sim_f   <- d_chat_similarity |> filter(gameID %in% kept_games)
```

## 2. The signed dimension index

The published analysis (`02_cogsci2025_analyses.qmd:532`) computes, for each
shape, how similar its descriptions are to descriptions of shapes sharing its
top versus shapes sharing its bottom, then takes

```r
sim_diff = abs(`bottom-match` - `top-match`)
```

The `abs()` is what this notebook removes. The **signed** difference

```
dimension index = sim(top-match) - sim(bottom-match)
```

is a per-dyad measure of which component the dyad indexes on. A top-indexer
describes A2, A3, A4 the same way (high top-match similarity) and C2, A2
differently (low bottom-match similarity), giving a large positive index. A
balanced compositional dyad names both components and the index sits near zero.
A holistic dyad has low similarity on both sides, also near zero — so the index
alone does not separate balanced from holistic, which is why §3 looks at mean
and variance separately and §4 adds a lexical measure.

```{r build-index}
d_sim_full <- d_sim_f |>
  left_join(d_round_f |> select(roundID1 = roundID, target1 = target,
                                index1 = index, repNum1 = repNum),
            by = "roundID1") |>
  left_join(d_round_f |> select(roundID2 = roundID, target2 = target,
                                index2 = index, repNum2 = repNum),
            by = "roundID2") |>
  left_join(d_game_f |> select(gameID, contextStructure_f), by = "gameID") |>
  mutate(top1    = str_extract(target1, "(?<=/)[^/]+(?=_)"),
         top2    = str_extract(target2, "(?<=/)[^/]+(?=_)"),
         bottom1 = str_extract(target1, "(?<=_)[^_]+(?=\\.png)"),
         bottom2 = str_extract(target2, "(?<=_)[^_]+(?=\\.png)"))

# The similarity file stores each pair once; mirror it so every round appears
# as roundID1. Matches the swap-and-bind in 02_cogsci2025_analyses.qmd:489.
swapped <- d_sim_full |>
  rename_with(~ paste0(., "_tmp"), ends_with("1")) |>
  rename_with(~ sub("2$", "1", .), ends_with("2")) |>
  rename_with(~ sub("1_tmp$", "2", .), ends_with("1_tmp"))

sim_pairs <- bind_rows(d_sim_full, swapped) |>
  filter(roundID1 != roundID2)

# Within-block pairs of *different* shapes, labelled by what they share.
# case_when order matters only for pairs sharing both components, which cannot
# occur in a 4x4 matrix once target1 != target2.
subshape_pairs <- sim_pairs |>
  filter(repNum1 == repNum2, target1 != target2) |>
  mutate(match = case_when(top1 == top2    ~ "top_match",
                           bottom1 == bottom2 ~ "bottom_match",
                           TRUE               ~ "non_match"))

shape_sim <- subshape_pairs |>
  filter(match != "non_match") |>
  group_by(gameID, contextStructure_f, repNum1, target1, match) |>
  summarize(mean_sim = mean(similarity, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = match, values_from = mean_sim) |>
  filter(!is.na(top_match), !is.na(bottom_match)) |>
  mutate(dim_index = top_match - bottom_match,   # signed: the new quantity
         abs_index = abs(dim_index))              # published quantity
```

### Sanity check against the published result

Before interpreting anything, confirm that the unsigned version reproduces the
published coefficients: Across Trial starts higher (β ≈ 0.069) and grows over
blocks (β ≈ 0.054), Within Trial flat (β ≈ 0.001, *p* = .78). If this does not
reproduce, the pipeline is wrong and §3–§5 are meaningless.

```{r sanity}
abs_model <- lmer(abs_index ~ contextStructure_f * repNum1 + (1 | gameID),
                  data = shape_sim |>
                    filter(contextStructure_f != "No Competitor") |>
                    mutate(contextStructure_f =
                             relevel(droplevels(contextStructure_f),
                                     ref = "Within Trial")))

tidy(abs_model, effects = "fixed") |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 4))) |>
  kable(caption = "Unsigned index — should reproduce the published Fig. 4 model")
```

No Competitor is dropped from every model below. With components paired 1:1
there are no component-sharing pairs, so neither `top_match` nor `bottom_match`
is defined. This is not a missing-data problem; it is the design.

## 3. Test 1 — distribution of the signed index

The model (§2.6) says the across-trial tie between `u_T` and `u_B` is broken by
accumulated strength alone, so each dyad commits to a dimension: arbitrary
*between* dyads, stable *within* dyad.

The diagnostic separates the **mean** from the **variance**, because the
published unsigned result already guarantees a larger spread in across-trial.
Larger variance alone is therefore not evidence of anything.

- **Commitment**: population mean ≈ 0, dyad-level SD large.
- **Population-level salience bias**: mean ≫ 0 (or ≪ 0). The model would then
  need the free dimension prior flagged in §5, and "arbitrary" is wrong.
- **No commitment**: mean ≈ 0 and SD small.

```{r test1-dyad-index}
dyad_index <- shape_sim |>
  filter(contextStructure_f != "No Competitor") |>
  group_by(gameID, contextStructure_f) |>
  summarize(dim_index = mean(dim_index, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_shapes  = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(contextStructure_f = droplevels(contextStructure_f))

dyad_index_final <- shape_sim |>
  filter(contextStructure_f != "No Competitor", repNum1 == FINAL_BLOCK) |>
  group_by(gameID, contextStructure_f) |>
  summarize(dim_index = mean(dim_index, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(contextStructure_f = droplevels(contextStructure_f))

bind_rows(
  dyad_index       |> mutate(window = "all blocks"),
  dyad_index_final |> mutate(window = "final block")
) |>
  group_by(window, contextStructure_f) |>
  summarize(n = n(),
            mean  = mean(dim_index),
            sd    = sd(dim_index),
            mean_abs = mean(abs(dim_index)),
            prop_top_indexing = mean(dim_index > 0),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 4))) |>
  kable(caption = "Mean vs SD of the signed index. Commitment predicts mean near 0 with large SD in Across Trial.")
```

Is the mean distinguishable from zero, and is the dyad-level SD larger in
across-trial? The second is a variance-ratio test; the first is a one-sample
test per condition.

```{r test1-tests}
dyad_index_final |>
  group_by(contextStructure_f) |>
  summarize(t = list(broom::tidy(t.test(dim_index))), .groups = "drop") |>
  unnest(t) |>
  select(contextStructure_f, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, p.value) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 4))) |>
  kable(caption = "Is the population mean index zero? (final block)")

var.test(dim_index ~ contextStructure_f, data = dyad_index_final)
```

### Bimodality

Hand-rolled bimodality coefficient so the notebook has no new dependencies.
`BC > 0.555` is the conventional flag. Hartigan's dip test is the better
instrument and runs if `diptest` is installed.

```{r test1-bimodality}
bimodality_coef <- function(x) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  n <- length(x)
  if (n < 4) return(NA_real_)
  m <- mean(x); s <- sd(x)
  skew <- sum((x - m)^3) / (n * s^3)
  kurt <- sum((x - m)^4) / (n * s^4) - 3
  (skew^2 + 1) / (kurt + 3 * (n - 1)^2 / ((n - 2) * (n - 3)))
}

dyad_index_final |>
  group_by(contextStructure_f) |>
  summarize(n = n(),
            bimodality_coef = round(bimodality_coef(dim_index), 3),
            dip_p = if (requireNamespace("diptest", quietly = TRUE)) {
              round(diptest::dip.test(dim_index)$p.value, 4)
            } else NA_real_,
            .groups = "drop") |>
  kable(caption = "Bimodality. BC > 0.555 is the conventional threshold.")

if (!requireNamespace("diptest", quietly = TRUE)) {
  message("For Hartigan's dip test: install.packages('diptest')")
}
```

```{r test1-plot}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4
p_dist <- dyad_index_final |>
  ggplot(aes(x = dim_index, fill = contextStructure_f)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, alpha = .85, colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey30") +
  facet_wrap(~ contextStructure_f) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = color_map, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "sim(top-match) - sim(bottom-match)",
       y = "Dyads",
       title = "Signed dimension index, final block",
       subtitle = "Commitment predicts two modes away from zero in Across Trial")

p_dist
ggsave(file.path(fig_path, "dim_index_distribution.png"), p_dist,
       width = 9, height = 4, dpi = 300)
```

## 4. Test 2 — does early commitment predict late commitment?

The magnitude-robust test. Rich-get-richer says the dimension a dyad lands on
early should be the one it keeps, and that the lock-in is stronger in
across-trial, where nothing but accumulation breaks the tie. In within-trial
both dimensions are forced, so there is less to lock in.

Two measures: the correlation of block-1 with block-4 index, and plain sign
agreement (which does not scale with effect magnitude).

```{r test2}
by_block <- shape_sim |>
  filter(contextStructure_f != "No Competitor",
         repNum1 %in% c(0, FINAL_BLOCK)) |>
  group_by(gameID, contextStructure_f, repNum1) |>
  summarize(dim_index = mean(dim_index, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(block = if_else(repNum1 == 0, "block1", "block4")) |>
  select(-repNum1) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = block, values_from = dim_index) |>
  filter(!is.na(block1), !is.na(block4)) |>
  mutate(contextStructure_f = droplevels(contextStructure_f),
         sign_agree = sign(block1) == sign(block4))

by_block |>
  group_by(contextStructure_f) |>
  summarize(n = n(),
            pearson  = round(cor(block1, block4), 3),
            spearman = round(cor(block1, block4, method = "spearman"), 3),
            prop_sign_agree = round(mean(sign_agree), 3),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  kable(caption = "Block 1 -> block 4 stability. Commitment predicts higher values in Across Trial.")

# Sign agreement against chance, per condition
by_block |>
  group_by(contextStructure_f) |>
  summarize(b = list(broom::tidy(binom.test(sum(sign_agree), n()))),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  unnest(b) |>
  select(contextStructure_f, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, p.value) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 4))) |>
  kable(caption = "Sign agreement vs. 0.5 chance")

# Does condition moderate the early->late relationship?
summary(lm(block4 ~ block1 * contextStructure_f, data = by_block))
```

Low-magnitude dyads contribute mostly noise to sign agreement, so split by
how strongly the dyad indexes at all.

```{r test2-by-magnitude}
by_block |>
  mutate(magnitude = ntile(abs(block1), 3),
         magnitude = factor(magnitude, labels = c("weak", "mid", "strong"))) |>
  group_by(contextStructure_f, magnitude) |>
  summarize(n = n(), prop_sign_agree = round(mean(sign_agree), 3),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  kable(caption = "Sign agreement by block-1 index magnitude")
```

```{r test2-plot}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4
p_stability <- by_block |>
  ggplot(aes(x = block1, y = block4, colour = contextStructure_f)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey70") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey70") +
  geom_point(alpha = .5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = color_map, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Dimension index, block 1", y = "Dimension index, block 4",
       title = "Does a dyad keep the dimension it started with?")

p_stability
ggsave(file.path(fig_path, "dim_index_stability.png"), p_stability,
       width = 7, height = 4, dpi = 300)
```

## 5. Test 3 — dedicated component labels (lexical, no embeddings)

An independent measure of the same claim that uses no embeddings at all, so
R2's objection to similarity measures does not reach it (`model-design.md` §3,
design doc §3 item 6).

A component has a **dedicated label** for a dyad if some word appears in the
dyad's final-block descriptions of at least two shapes containing that
component, and in no description of a shape lacking it. Counting dedicated
components per dyad estimates the size of its primitive lexicon.

Model predictions (`model-design.md` §1.2): **Within Trial ≈ 8** dedicated
components, **Across Trial ≈ 4 and concentrated on one role**, and the measure
is **structurally undefined for No Competitor** — each component appears in
exactly one shape, so `n_with ≥ 2` is unreachable. That last point is the
vocabulary-cost argument, not a null result, and is reported as such.

```{r test3-tokens}
#| message: false
stop_words_small <- c(
  "the","a","an","and","or","but","if","then","than","that","this","these",
  "those","is","are","was","were","be","been","being","it","its","of","to",
  "in","on","at","by","for","with","from","as","into","like","looks","look",
  "shape","shapes","one","two","side","sides","has","have","there","thing",
  "kind","sort","bit","more","most","very","really","sort","i","you","we",
  "think","maybe","something","left","right","top","bottom","upper","lower"
)

final_msgs <- d_chat_f |>
  filter(as.character(director_msg) == "TRUE",
         as.character(chit_chat) == "FALSE") |>
  inner_join(d_round_f |> select(roundID, gameID, target, repNum),
             by = "roundID") |>
  filter(repNum == FINAL_BLOCK) |>
  group_by(gameID, target) |>
  summarize(text = paste(text, collapse = " "), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(d_game_f |> select(gameID, contextStructure_f), by = "gameID") |>
  mutate(top    = str_extract(target, "(?<=/)[^/]+(?=_)"),
         bottom = str_extract(target, "(?<=_)[^_]+(?=\\.png)"))

tokens <- final_msgs |>
  mutate(word = str_split(str_to_lower(text), "[^a-z]+")) |>
  unnest(word) |>
  filter(nchar(word) >= 3, !word %in% stop_words_small) |>
  distinct(gameID, contextStructure_f, target, top, bottom, word)

cat("Dyads with final-block descriptions:", n_distinct(tokens$gameID), "\n")
```

```{r test3-dedicated}
# Long form: one row per (dyad, shape, component role, component id, word)
shape_components <- tokens |>
  pivot_longer(c(top, bottom), names_to = "role", values_to = "component")

# For each (dyad, role, component, word): shapes containing the component that
# use the word, vs shapes lacking it that use the word.
n_with <- shape_components |>
  count(gameID, contextStructure_f, role, component, word, name = "n_with")

# Total uses of each word by the dyad, per role, to derive n_without
n_total <- shape_components |>
  distinct(gameID, role, target, word) |>
  count(gameID, role, word, name = "n_total")

dedicated <- n_with |>
  left_join(n_total, by = c("gameID", "role", "word")) |>
  mutate(n_without = n_total - n_with,
         is_dedicated = n_with >= 2 & n_without == 0)

component_level <- dedicated |>
  group_by(gameID, contextStructure_f, role, component) |>
  summarize(has_dedicated = any(is_dedicated), .groups = "drop")

dyad_lexicon <- component_level |>
  group_by(gameID, contextStructure_f, role) |>
  summarize(n_dedicated = sum(has_dedicated), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = role, values_from = n_dedicated,
              names_prefix = "dedicated_", values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(lexicon_size = dedicated_top + dedicated_bottom,
         lexical_commitment = if_else(
           lexicon_size > 0,
           (dedicated_top - dedicated_bottom) / lexicon_size,
           NA_real_))

dyad_lexicon |>
  group_by(contextStructure_f) |>
  summarize(n = n(),
            mean_dedicated_top    = round(mean(dedicated_top), 2),
            mean_dedicated_bottom = round(mean(dedicated_bottom), 2),
            mean_lexicon_size     = round(mean(lexicon_size), 2),
            mean_abs_commitment   = round(mean(abs(lexical_commitment),
                                               na.rm = TRUE), 3),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  kable(caption = "Dedicated component labels per dyad. Predicted: Within ~8, Across ~4 on one role, No Competitor structurally 0.")
```

Within-trial descriptions are longer, which mechanically affords more
candidate words. Report length alongside, and covary it.

```{r test3-length-control}
dyad_length <- final_msgs |>
  mutate(n_words = str_count(text, "\\S+")) |>
  group_by(gameID) |>
  summarize(mean_words = mean(n_words), .groups = "drop")

lex_model_data <- dyad_lexicon |>
  left_join(dyad_length, by = "gameID") |>
  filter(contextStructure_f != "No Competitor") |>
  mutate(contextStructure_f = relevel(droplevels(contextStructure_f),
                                      ref = "Within Trial"))

summary(lm(lexicon_size ~ contextStructure_f + scale(mean_words),
           data = lex_model_data))
```

### Cross-validation: do the lexical and embedding measures agree?

The strongest version of §5. `lexical_commitment` and `dim_index` are computed
from disjoint information — word identity versus SBERT similarity. If both say
the same dyads index tops, that is hard to get by accident.

```{r test3-crossvalidate}
crossval <- dyad_lexicon |>
  inner_join(dyad_index_final, by = c("gameID", "contextStructure_f")) |>
  filter(!is.na(lexical_commitment))

crossval |>
  group_by(contextStructure_f) |>
  summarize(n = n(),
            pearson = round(cor(lexical_commitment, dim_index), 3),
            spearman = round(cor(lexical_commitment, dim_index,
                                 method = "spearman"), 3),
            sign_agree = round(mean(sign(lexical_commitment) ==
                                      sign(dim_index)), 3),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  kable(caption = "Agreement between the lexical and embedding indices")
```

```{r test3-plot}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4
#| warning: false
p_crossval <- crossval |>
  ggplot(aes(x = lexical_commitment, y = dim_index,
             colour = contextStructure_f)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey70") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey70") +
  geom_jitter(width = .03, alpha = .55) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = color_map, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Lexical commitment  (dedicated tops - bottoms) / total",
       y = "Embedding dimension index",
       title = "Two independent measures of the same claim")

p_crossval
ggsave(file.path(fig_path, "dim_index_crossvalidation.png"), p_crossval,
       width = 7, height = 4, dpi = 300)
```

## 6. Annotation gold set

The 478 hand-coded items are only ~10 dyads per condition and cover final-round
descriptions only, so they cannot carry Test 1 or Test 2. They do provide a
validity check: dyads the annotations call top-only versus bottom-only should
fall on the corresponding side of `dim_index`.

```{r annotations}
#| message: false
annot_files <- list.files(file.path(data_root, "annotation_data"),
                          pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)

d_annot <- map_dfr(annot_files, read.csv) |>
  inner_join(d_round_f |> select(roundID, gameID, repNum), by = "roundID") |>
  left_join(d_game_f |> select(gameID, contextStructure_f), by = "gameID") |>
  filter(annotation != "idk")

cat("Annotated items:", nrow(d_annot),
    "across", n_distinct(d_annot$gameID), "dyads\n")

annot_commitment <- d_annot |>
  filter(annotation %in% c("top", "bottom")) |>
  group_by(gameID, contextStructure_f) |>
  summarize(n_single = n(),
            annot_top_share = mean(annotation == "top"), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n_single >= 3)

annot_commitment |>
  inner_join(dyad_index, by = c("gameID", "contextStructure_f")) |>
  group_by(contextStructure_f) |>
  summarize(n = n(),
            cor_with_dim_index = round(cor(annot_top_share, dim_index), 3),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  kable(caption = "Annotator-coded top share vs. embedding index (small n; validity check only)")
```

## 7. Verdict

Fill this in after running. The model-design decisions each test can falsify:

| Test | Supports §2.6 if | Falsifies §2.6 if |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Distribution | Across Trial mean ≈ 0, SD large, BC > 0.555 | SD comparable to Within Trial, or mean far from 0 (a population salience bias, not commitment) |
| 2. Block 1 → 4 | sign agreement ≫ .5 and higher than Within Trial | agreement ≈ .5, i.e. the dimension is re-chosen each block |
| 3. Dedicated labels | Across ≈ 4 concentrated on one role; Within ≈ 8 balanced | Across ≈ 8, or no role concentration |
| Cross-validation | lexical and embedding indices agree in sign | no relationship — one of the two measures is not measuring commitment |

A unimodal across-trial distribution with sign agreement at chance falsifies
the rich-get-richer credit rule in `model-design.md` §2.6, and with it the
asymmetric-generalization prediction in §6. That outcome should be recorded
here and the model revised before any simulation code is written.
